//: Story Phase 7, chapter 33: It's Coming Back. Two days after the Frog Grog Offensive. Repairs, complaints, the second cloud still in the sleeping quarters, the Grand Stenchmaster in his chair facing a broken television. Then Ned, at the bow: the storm on the horizon is getting bigger. Environmental progression: the dark rotating cloud through the telescope, then fins in the air, then yellow-tinged spray on the deck. It is the SAME storm, coming back (not re-formed: no formation scene). 'Didn't we destroy that thing?' 'Technically, we discouraged it.' The bulk Frog Grog is gone. THWACK: the first shark on the deck again. Squawks: 'No.' 'I know.' And the Grand Stenchmaster Aura.

start: Your bed. The yellow outline on the pillow has been joined by a smaller, sharper one, in the shape of a cloud of garlic.

p7c1.begin.narrate: Two days of patching, splicing, scrubbing, and arguing about who was going to sleep where, since the sleeping quarters still belonged to the second cloud.
The storm was still out there, on the horizon. Everybody had stopped looking at it. That was the arrangement.

p7c1.deck: A grey morning. The deck is a mess of splintered planks and storm wreckage. Somebody is hammering. Somebody else is complaining about the hammering.
hale[resigned]: Morning, Captain. Repairs are coming along. Slowly. Everything we fix, something else falls off.
hale: The debris midships needs clearing, and Finch could use a hand with the fore shrouds. They took a beating.
From the station, without turning round, the Grand Stenchmaster sighs heavily at the broken television, for the forty-first time this morning.
hale: He's been sitting there since dawn. Staring at it. Like it owes him money.

p7c1.deck.tutorial: Help with the repairs: the storm debris (midships, by the mainmast) and the fore shrouds (the foremast, forward).
p7c1.deck.title: It's Coming Back

p7c1.debris: A heap of splintered rail, a snarl of line, a lot of seaweed and, inexplicably, a tooth.
gristle: Lift on three, Captain. Mind the tooth. It's not mine.
Over the side it goes. Most of it.
gristle[annoyed]: Two days. Two DAYS I've been clearing this deck, and it still smells like the inside of a boot that's been inside a shark.
gristle: And the grog. Don't get me started on the grog. Mags's new batch tastes like the old batch with regret in it.

then.text: CAPTAIN! CAPTAIN, COME AND LOOK AT THIS!

then.tutorial: Ned's shouting from the bow. See what he wants.
then.title: It's Coming Back

p7c1.foremast: The fore shrouds, half re-rove, slack and fraying where the storm had them.
finch: Haul when I say, Captain. Haul... now!
finch[happy]: There. Tight as Jim's purse.
finch: Sails are another matter. Every one of them's stained yellow up to the reefs. We look like a floating custard.

then.text: CAPTAIN! CAPTAIN, COME AND LOOK AT THIS!

then.tutorial: Ned's shouting from the bow. See what he wants.
then.title: It's Coming Back

p7c1.ned: Ned is at the very bow, as far forward as anyone can go, staring out to starboard.
ned[concerned]: Captain. You know how the storm's been on the horizon? Over there? Not doing anything?
ned[concerned]: It's... bigger, Captain. Isn't it?
ned: I keep looking at it and telling myself it's further away. And then I look again.
ned[concerned]: Aye. Course it is. ...Would you look anyway? Through the glass?

p7c1.ned.tutorial: Look at the horizon through the telescope (starboard, by the forward rail).
p7c1.ned.title: It's Coming Back

p7c1.telescope: You put the telescope to your eye and find the horizon. Grey sea. Grey sea. Grey—
The same mustard smudge as two days ago. The same thin dark thread down to the sea.
Except it isn't a smudge any more. It's a column. It's turning, and you can see it turning.
And it's bigger every time you blink.
You lower the telescope. You don't need it any more.
Something goes over the ship. High. Very high. Fins. In the air. Going the wrong way for fins.
Spray comes over the starboard rail and spatters across the deck. You wipe it off your face. It's warm. It's yellow.
p7c1.realise: By the time you're back aft, the whole crew is at the starboard rail. Nobody is hammering any more.
pete[alarmed]: Didn't we DESTROY that thing?
rook[alarmed]: We threw SIXTEEN BARRELS at it!
bob[concerned]: It fell down. I watched it fall down. It fell down like a curtain.
From his chair, not getting up, the Grand Stenchmaster raises one gloved finger.
garrick[businesslike]: Technically, we discouraged it.
crew: YOU SAID IT WAS GONE!
garrick[businesslike]: Forecasting language is nuanced.
pete[annoyed]: NUANCED?
garrick: 'Driven off.' Off. Not 'destroyed'. Off is a direction. Directions can be reversed.
rook[annoyed]: Somebody hold my coat.
hale[concerned]: It's the sea, Captain. The sea's still yellow for miles. The air's still... the air. And there's still hundreds of sharks behind us. Every one of them still following the smell.
hale: We broke it up. We didn't take any of it away. It's had two days to pull itself back together.
You turn round, slowly, and look at the bulk Frog Grog lashings by the starboard rail.
Empty. Sixteen ropes, tied round nothing.
captain[alarmed]: ...Mags. The grog. How much have we got?
mags[concerned]: In bulk? Nothing, Captain. You know that. It all went into that.
mags: I've two small casks brewing and they're not ready, and if they were it wouldn't be enough to annoy a rowboat.
captain[alarmed]: Then we can't do it again.
mags[concerned]: No, Captain. We can't do it again.
You stare at the empty lashings. Two days ago you rolled the whole reserve into the sea, cheering. All of it. For this.
p7c1.thwack: A shark. On the deck. Again. Right in front of the cabin door, flopping.
Another one sails over the mainmast. Then another, lower.
The one on the deck flops twice and throws itself back over the rail, as if it, too, would rather be anywhere else.
In his basket by the cabin door, a small bald head comes up out of the blankets, and looks at the sky.
p7c1.aura: From the Grand Stenchmaster's chair, a tiny pale wisp drifts up, curls, and is gone.
garrick[proud]: That, gentlemen, is residual Stenchmaster exhaust. Perfectly normal after a historic event. It'll taper off over the next few—
captain[angry]: I forbid it. The phrase. Never again. Not on this ship.
garrick[businesslike]: ...Very well, Captain. Let's call it the Grand Stenchmaster Aura.
